newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine raises planned T-bill sales volume.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine raises planned T-bill sales volume.

text.p: The Ukrainian government has nearly doubled the amount of Treasury bills it plans to sell this year, for which no budget has yet been passed, to six billion hrvynias from 3.5 billion hryvnias, its press service said on Monday.
A spokeswoman said the decision was taken because by May 8 the authorities had sold off the entire 3.5 billion hryvnias of paper which it had previously said would be sold this year.
This year's budget has yet to be approved so the government has been topping up the forecast level of issues for the year.
Ukraine's T-bill sales proved so popular with non-residents they have helped support the hryvnia, introduced on September 2.
The finance ministry has been selling T-bills this year with maturities of three, six, nine and 12 months.
But in all it has the right to issue paper with maturities of 28, 63, 91, 182 and 273 days, one year, 18 months and two or three years.

Average yields on six-month paper edged down to 27.01 percent from 28.36 percent on May 8 and to 28.99 percent from 30.85 percent on nine-month paper and on 12-month bills to 32.98 percent from 34.32 percent.

An official at the finance ministry's ssecurities department told Reuters that five million hryvnias worth of three-month paper, nine million in six-month, 24 million in nine-month and 31 million hryvnias in annual paper would be sold on May 13.
